column1: # Half the rows are forms a per-character method gets WRONG, half are controls it gets
# RIGHT. The controls are the point: a test set of only hard cases would show that the
# dictionary fires, not that it fires in the right places. A dictionary that "corrected"
# 菩薩 or 涅槃 — which need no correction — would be worse than none.
# `naive` is Unihan's kMandarin reading applied character by character, which is what a
# generic pinyin library does. It is recorded here so the comparison is reproducible and
# so a change in Unicode shows up as a test failure rather than a silent drift.
